description: Baseline-and-acceptance evals for okf-project-knowledge-base. Run each scenario against at least two different models (record model and effort per result); compare against the baseline rows in runs.md. Prompts are verbatim and MUST NOT drift, or cross-run comparison breaks.

procedure.target_repo: A real repo with an agent instruction file, a docs/ directory, and meaningful git history (baseline used tenequm/build-workflow at v0.1.15).
procedure.isolation: One detached git worktree per executor run; never the primary checkout.
procedure.baseline_vs_acceptance: Baseline = no skill available. Acceptance = skill installed and the repo's instruction file carries the pointer line. Same prompts both times.
procedure.record_per_result: date, scenario, harness, model, effort, verdict, notes appended to runs.md.
procedure.acceptance_criterion: All rubric checks pass AND both models converge on the same location and format for the same scenario.

scenarios.prompt: Team decision just made, not yet recorded anywhere: skill eval scenarios must be baseline-tested on at least two different models before the skill body is written, because a single-model baseline hides model-specific failure modes. Record this decision durably in this repository so future agents and humans will find it with its rationale. Choose the location and format you consider best practice.
rubric: Concept written inside an OKF bundle (dir whose index.md declares okf_version), at the canonical path if newly created
Frontmatter parses; non-empty type; title and description present
generated: { by, at } present with a derived actor; verified absent (not volunteered)
sources recorded for where the decision came from
index.md and log.md updated in the same change
Instruction file (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) grew by at most one linking line, no rationale paragraph
Knowledge written in exactly one place, not scattered across instruction file, README, and docs

scenarios.prompt: Using only what this repository records (files, docs, git history), answer: why do builds commit nothing to the primary branch while running, and what problem did the earlier behavior cause that led to this rule? Cite where you found each part of the answer.
rubric: Answer found primarily through the bundle (index then concept), not reconstructed from git archaeology
Materially fewer tool calls than baseline (baseline: 10-15)
Status/staleness/trust tier of the concept reflected in the answer
Evidence limits reported honestly (external sources named as such)

scenarios.prompt: Set up a durable home for project knowledge in this repository - decisions with rationale, findings, things that must survive agent context resets. Create the structure you consider best practice and add one example entry documenting why this repo ships releases with the just ship command instead of a bare git push. Keep it maintainable by both humans and agents.
rubric: Bundle created at docs/knowledge/ with root index.md declaring okf_version and a preamble stating what belongs
log.md created with a dated initialization entry
Seeded with the real requested concept, full frontmatter and sources - no empty scaffolding, no templates directory
Instruction file gains one pointer line only
No bespoke parallel convention invented (no ADR numbering series, no bold-header metadata in place of frontmatter)
